newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KEY EURO 96 TRIO RETURN TO GERMANY SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY EURO 96 TRIO RETURN TO GERMANY SQUAD.

text.p: Germany coach Berti Vogts has brought three key Euro 96 players back into his squad after injury for next month's crunch World Cup qualifier against Portugal.

Libero Matthias Sammer, defender Thomas Helmer and wing-back Christian Ziege, who all missed the European champions' frustrating 1-1 draw at home with Northern Ireland earlier this month, were named in a provisional 28-man party on Wednesday.

Bayern Munich's in-form midfielder Mario Basler, who was part of the Euro 96 squad but did not make an impact because of injury, also returned to the party for the European group nine clash in Lisbon on December 14.

But Vogts said it was a major blow that he was unable to call on Karlsruhe's veteran midfielder Thomas Haessler, who could be out of action for three months after picking up a serious ankle injury in a league match last Friday.
"That is tough for us. Thomas is the best player in Germany at the moment and perhaps even the best player in his position in Europe," the German coach said.
The Portuguese have a special place in the history of German soccer. They are the only team ever to have beaten the Germans in a World Cup qualifier, winning 1-0 in Stuttgart in October 1985.
But the Germans have not lost to Portugal since and beat them 2-1 in a friendly in Porto in February.

Vogts held a squad session for prospective internationals earlier this week and named nine of them in the party which will be cut back after the last round of league matches, on December 7, before the Bundesliga's winter break.
Vogts was very impressed with Bayern's uncapped striker Alexander Zickler whom he sees as a good partner for Juergen Klinsmann.

Zickler was included in the squad but, with the competition up front so fierce, he will probably have to wait for his chance to join the Germany captain in attack. "He is the perfect club partner for Klinsmann," Vogts said. "There is a lot to come out of him yet."
Bayer Leverkusen striker Ulf Kirsten's superb form in recent games was also rewarded with a place in the party.
Goalkeepers: Oliver Kahn (Bayern Munich), Andreas Koepke (Marseille), Oliver Reck (Werder Bremen)

Defenders: Markus Babbel, Thomas Helmer (both Bayern), Juergen Kohler (Borussia Dortmund), Stephan Passlack (Borussia Moenchengladbach), Stefan Reuter, Matthias Sammer (both Dortmund), Christian Woerns (Bayer Leverkusen)

Midfielders: Mario Basler (Bayern), Marco Bode, Dieter Eilts (both Werder Bremen), Thorsten Fink (Karlsruhe), Matthias Hagner (VfB Stuttgart), Joerg Heinrich (Dortmund), Sven Kmetsch (Hamburg), Andy Moeller (Dortmund), Thomas Strunz (Bayern), Michael Tarnat (Karlsruhe), Dariusz Wosz (Bochum), Christian Ziege (Bayern)
Forwards: Oliver Bierhoff (Udinese), Fredi Bobic (Stuttgart), Heiko Herrlich (Dortmund), Ulf Kirsten (Leverkusen), Juergen Klinsmann, Alexander Zickler (both Bayern).
